rationale: The claim's nominal expected file tables/tables/Table4.tex holds the AUTHORS' original Stata output (incumbent 0.095/0.055/0.422, new entrant 0.019/0.023/-0.178 — identical to the paper), which cannot be this run's product: the R port's own reproduction (replication_log.json step 4 stdout 'incumbent(m1) %dW=0.067 spillover=0.511; new-entrant(m2) %dW=0.042 spillover=0.073', step 7, and the run-produced tables/dofiles/Table4.tex + logs/table4_groups.csv) got different incumbent/new-entrant numbers. Grading the run-produced evidence: the Overall + 5 demographic rows match the paper to the printed precision — Overall 0.068/0.041/0.397, HSD 0.077/0.048/0.370, teen 0.081/0.053/0.347, HSL 0.073/0.043/0.402, female 0.070/0.045/0.359, BH 0.045/0.037/0.179 (BH shown non-significant and smaller, as the paper reports) — 18 of 30 cells within 5%. However: (a) the Tradeable and Nontradeable rows were never computed — rport/groups.R only defines groups overall/HSD/HSL/teen/female/BH, so paper values 0.058/0.065/-0.114 and 0.056/0.043/0.237 have no produced counterpart; (b) Incumbent 0.067/0.033/0.511 deviates from paper 0.095/0.055/0.422 by ~30%/40%/21%; (c) New entrant 0.042/0.038/0.073 deviates from paper 0.019/0.023/-0.178 by >60% with the spillover share flipping sign (small positive vs the paper's -0.178). The run's step-7 note acknowledges the incumbent/new-entrant divergence, attributing it to omitted placebo controls / far-above bins not shipped as columns; fix_severity.json also flags the Stata→R port as load-checked but not numerically validated. Directionally the qualitative story holds (spillovers ~40% overall, smaller for Black/Hispanic, incumbents > new entrants), but the tradeable and new-entrant near-zero/negative shares specified in the verification instruction were not reproduced (tradeable absent; new entrant positive 0.073). Mixed cells → partial.
